extracted_data.name_full: Anharmonic lattice dynamics / phonon Boltzmann transport equation computed with phono3py using DFT or HDNNP-predicted forces
extracted_data.brief_description: The paper uses phono3py to compute second- and third-order IFCs (finite-displacement) and solve the linearized phonon BTE in the single-mode RTA to obtain lattice thermal conductivity, with forces supplied either by DFT (VASP) or by an HDNNP trained to DFT forces.
extracted_data.material_system: Applied to Si and GaN in this work (Si bulk crystal and GaN bulk crystal).
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: bulk crystals (Si conventional cell; GaN primitive cell specified for supercells in phonon calculations).
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: κ(T) calculated and plotted in Figure 3 for Si (see Fig.3a) and GaN (Fig.3b,c); paper highlights accuracy ranges of 200–500 K for Si and 200–1000 K for GaN (relative HDNNP vs DFT agreement).
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: See material-specific entries: for Si κ(300 K)=112.1 W/m·K (DFT) and 110.4 W/m·K (HDNNP). For GaN (example): in-plane κ_parallel(300 K) = 274.2 W/m·K (DFT) vs 275.5 W/m·K (HDNNP); out-of-plane κ_perp(300 K) = 325.5 W/m·K (DFT) vs 309.7 W/m·K (HDNNP). Paper reports HDNNP deviation within 5.4% for GaN across 200–1000 K.
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity from phonon BTE; lifetimes computed from three-phonon interactions via third-order IFCs; single-mode RTA used (no electronic contribution).
extracted_data.method_category: first-principles PBTE/ALD (DFT IFCs) and hybrid (HDNNP substituted for DFT to supply forces/IFCs).
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: Brillouin-zone q-grid for BTE: 11×11×11 in all cases. Second-order IFC supercells: Si 2×2×2 (conventional), GaN 3×3×2 (primitive). Third-order IFC supercells: Si 2×2×2 (conventional), GaN 2×2×2 (primitive). DFT displacement counts: Si 111 displacement patterns; GaN 582 displacements. HDNNP dramatically reduces force-evaluation time for these displacement calculations.
extracted_data.first_principles_details: DFT via VASP (PAW). Exchange–correlation: LDA for Si, GGA-PBE for GaN. Plane-wave cutoff: 550 eV. IFCs obtained by finite-displacement using phonopy/phono3py. Non-analytic LO–TO corrections were not included in GaN phonon dispersion calculations for the comparison.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon (third-order) processes included. Isotope scattering, four-phonon processes, boundary/size effects and electron–phonon scattering are not included or not mentioned. RTA (single-mode) approximation used rather than full iterative solution.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: Within-paper comparisons: HDNNP-derived forces vs direct DFT forces used in the same ALD/BTE workflow (phono3py); numerical agreement metrics: Si within 1% (200–500 K), GaN within 5.4% (200–1000 K). Computational speed comparisons reported (orders-of-magnitude speedup for HDNNP force evaluations).
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: Phonon dispersion comparisons to experiment are shown in Fig.2; thermal-conductivity results are compared to DFT benchmarks rather than directly to experimental κ data. The paper notes previous GaN κ results differ and attributes underestimation here to small IFC supercell size in this work.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Small IFC supercell sizes can underestimate κ (GaN example: 32-atom cell used here vs 108-atom cell in prior study). HDNNP neglects long-range electrostatic (explicitly stated) which may affect polar materials. Use of single-mode RTA instead of iterative BTE can produce differences. Training limitations of HDNNP (force RMSE) can cause residual discrepancies versus DFT.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Paper provides κ(T) curves and reports ranges of good HDNNP/DFT agreement (Si: 200–500 K; GaN: 200–1000 K). No explicit analytic temperature-scaling laws are fitted or reported in text.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Figures 2 (phonon dispersions) and 3 (thermal conductivity vs temperature for Si and GaN); methods and supercell sizes in main text and Supplementary Materials.

extracted_data.name_full: Crystalline diamond-structure silicon — first-principles DFT + Boltzmann Transport Equation (direct inversion) with quantum statistics
extracted_data.brief_description: First-principles PBTE calculation of lattice thermal conductivity of bulk diamond Si using DFPT second-order IFCs and finite-difference third-order IFCs, solving the linearized BTE by direct inversion and including quantum Bose–Einstein statistics for phonon populations.
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: diamond cubic, bulk crystalline
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: reported explicitly at 300 K; thermal conductivity vs temperature shown in Fig. 2 (range not numerically listed in text; qualitative curve comparing quantum/classical and RTA/inversion)
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: kappa_Q,Inv(300 K) = 147 W m^-1 K^-1 (quantum statistics, full inversion of scattering matrix); also plotted as function of T in Fig. 2.
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity (phonon-only). Quantum Bose–Einstein populations used; modal heat capacities and phonon lifetimes from anharmonic lattice dynamics (3-phonon Fermi Golden Rule). Reported as scalar (direction-averaged) bulk conductivity.
extracted_data.method_category: first-principles PBTE/DFT
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: Second- and third-order IFCs computed on supercells; phonon lifetimes & conductivity computed on a (19,19,19) q-point grid (BTE lifetimes/properties converged at this grid for presented result).
extracted_data.first_principles_details: DFT code: Quantum-Espresso (DFPT for 2nd order); functional: LDA; pseudopotential: Bachelet-Hamann-Schluter norm-conserving; plane-wave cutoff = 20 Ry; k-point mesh = (8,8,8); minimized lattice parameter = 5.398 Å. Third-order IFCs via finite-difference displacements on (5,5,5) replicas of irreducible fcc unit cell, including up to 5th nearest neighbor. BTE solved with both direct inversion and RTA; q-grid (19,19,19) used.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon scattering (Fermi Golden Rule) included; lifetimes from 3-phonon processes; quantum vs classical statistics considered. No explicit 4-phonon, isotope, electron-phonon, or boundary scattering reported for these calculations.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: Direct inversion (quantum) kappa = 147 W/mK; RTA (quantum) kappa = 140 W/mK (≈5% lower). Classical-limit direct inversion kappa_Cl,Inv = 123 W/mK and RTA kappa_Cl,RTA = 118 W/mK; quantum vs classical converge as T increases (see Fig.2).
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: Authors state kappa_Q,Inv = 147 W m^-1 K^-1 is in good agreement with experiment (experimental points shown in Fig.2 as light-blue x; refs cited).
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Differences between inversion and RTA arise because RTA neglects off-diagonal scattering terms; classical statistics reduce lifetimes (higher populations of high-frequency modes) and thus reduce kappa relative to quantum result at 300 K; hydrodynamic effects at low T make RTA less accurate.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Figure 2 shows kappa vs T: quantum and classical results converge at higher T; RTA underestimates kappa more strongly at low T where hydrodynamic effects become important. No explicit power-law fits given in text.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Section IV.A; Fig. 1 (mode-resolved properties at 300 K), Fig. 2 (thermal conductivity vs temperature); numerical value in text of Section IV.A.

extracted_data.name_full: Crystalline diamond-structure silicon — empirical Tersoff potential + ALD/BTE
extracted_data.brief_description: ALD/BTE calculations of thermal conductivity using IFCs obtained from the Tersoff empirical potential; shown to substantially overestimate kappa of diamond Si relative to DFT-based PBTE and experiment.
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: diamond cubic, bulk crystalline
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: reported at 300 K in text (no full curve provided for Tersoff in text besides mention that Fig.2 references quantum/classical results; Tersoff numbers quoted are at 300 K).
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: Using Tersoff: kappa_Q (300 K) = 305 W m^-1 K^-1 (quantum-statistics ALD) and kappa_Cl (300 K) = 260 W m^-1 K^-1 (classical limit) — substantial overestimation compared to DFT result.
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity (phonon-only), computed from ALD/BTE using IFCs from Tersoff; quantum and classical treatments reported.
extracted_data.method_category: empirical-potential ALD / PBTE (IFCs from empirical potential)
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff empirical potential (referenced as Tersoff ref. 48). Specific parameterization/version not detailed beyond 'Tersoff potential'.
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: Not all details enumerated for this Tersoff calculation in the text; statement references previous works reporting similar Tersoff results. For clathrate Tersoff calculations, explicit supercell and q-point details are given (see separate entry).
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon scattering via ALD; classical vs quantum statistics considered. No mention of 4-phonon or isotope scattering in this context.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: Tersoff (305 W/mK) vs DFT direct inversion (147 W/mK) at 300 K — Tersoff overestimates by roughly a factor ~2 for diamond Si. Also Tersoff classical 260 vs DFT classical 123 shows similar overestimate.
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: Authors indicate Tersoff results substantially overestimate experimental values; DFT result is in better agreement with experiment.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Inadequacy of empirical potential in reproducing phonon dispersion/anharmonicity and lifetimes leads to overestimated kappa; forcefield parametrization gives too weak scattering/higher group velocities compared to DFT and experiment.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Not detailed beyond 300 K comparisons and general remark that quantum/classical converge at high T.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Mentioned in Section IV.A (text) as comparison; earlier references to prior works reporting Tersoff values.

extracted_data.name_full: Pristine type-II Si136 silicon clathrate — IFCs from Tersoff potential, BTE solved in relaxation time approximation
extracted_data.brief_description: BTE-RTA calculation of thermal conductivity of type-II silicon clathrate (Si136) using second- and third-order IFCs from Tersoff; authors report modal properties and cumulative kappa at 300 K and compare to Ge-doped variants.
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: Type-II silicon clathrate, conventional cubic cell (136 atoms), crystalline
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: reported at 300 K (calculations described at 300 K); modal properties and cumulative kappa at 300 K shown in Fig.3.
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: kappa_BTE,RTA(300 K) = 101.3 W m^-1 K^-1 (Tersoff potential, BTE-RTA).
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity (phonon-only), computed within BTE-RTA using quantum statistics (300 K); modal decomposition (DOS, lifetimes, mean free paths) provided.
extracted_data.method_category: empirical-potential ALD / PBTE (IFCs from Tersoff) with BTE-RTA
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff empirical potential; short-range r_cut = 3.1 Å; second and third derivatives computed by finite differences over full interaction range of potential.
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: Calculations performed on conventional 136-atom cell. BTE used a (7,7,7) q-point grid deemed sufficiently dense to converge thermal conductivity. Third-order IFCs computed by finite differences on the 136-atom conventional cell.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon scattering (Fermi Golden Rule); quantum statistics used. Authors state corrections beyond RTA amount to less than 1% increase in kappa for this system (i.e., off-diagonal scattering small).
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: kappa(Si136, Tersoff, BTE-RTA) = 101.3 W/mK; authors note previous first-principles BTE studies reported ~50 W/mK at room temperature (so Tersoff overestimates relative to ab initio for this material as well).
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: No direct experimental comparison given for Si136 in this paper; authors compare to prior ab initio results.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Potential-dependent inaccuracies (Tersoff) and neglect of certain scattering in empirical parametrization likely cause higher kappa relative to ab initio BTE results. The authors explicitly note the Tersoff potential leads to overestimates in diamond Si and in clathrates compared to ab initio.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Reported at 300 K; no explicit temperature sweep presented for this system in text.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Section IV.B; Fig. 3 (panels a–e: DOS, phase-space, lifetimes, MFPs, cumulative kappa); Table I lists kappa = 101.3 W/mK for Si136 (BTE).

extracted_data.name_full: 15% Ge-substituted Type-II silicon clathrate (Si116Ge20) — Tersoff IFCs + BTE in RTA on 136-atom cell (random substitution)
extracted_data.brief_description: BTE-RTA calculation on 136-atom type-II clathrate with 20 Ge atoms substituted at random sites (15% Ge) using IFCs from Tersoff; reports large conductivity reduction and mode-resolved analysis at 300 K.
extracted_data.material_system: Si116Ge20 (Si0.85Ge0.15) Type-II clathrate (15% Ge substitution in 136-atom cell)
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: Type-II silicon clathrate conventional cell replicated (136 atoms) with random substitution of 20 Ge atoms (maintains crystalline periodicity within the conventional cell)
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: reported at 300 K (modal properties and cumulative kappa in Fig.3; numbers at 300 K).
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: kappa_BTE,RTA(300 K) = 33.0 W m^-1 K^-1 for Si116Ge20 (Tersoff, BTE-RTA on 136-atom cell).
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity (phonon-only), quantum statistics at 300 K, BTE-RTA solution.
extracted_data.method_category: empirical-potential ALD / PBTE (IFCs from Tersoff) with BTE-RTA
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff empirical potential (short-range r_cut = 3.1 Å); derivatives computed by finite differences over full interaction range.
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: 136-atom conventional cell used with randomly chosen substitution sites for Ge. BTE with (7,7,7) q-point grid. Authors state q-grid sufficient to converge kappa. For comparison with large supercells they replicate the 136-atom cell.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon scattering included (Fermi Golden Rule), with full IFCs from Tersoff (thus incorporating mass and force-constant disorder at the level present in that 136-atom periodic model). No explicit Tamura or mass-only scattering term used.
extracted_data.alloy_modeling_approach: Explicit substitution of Ge at random sites within the 136-atom conventional cell (so includes both mass and local force-constant changes within that periodic cell).
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: Si136 pristine (Tersoff BTE-RTA) = 101.3 W/mK; Si116Ge20 (same method) = 33.0 W/mK (~3× reduction). QHGK on replicated system gives 31.0 W/mK (see separate result), indicating close agreement for the replicated alloy cell between methods when size effects accounted for.
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: No direct experimental data for this substituted clathrate is provided in this paper.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Reduction in kappa attributed to symmetry breaking from Ge substitutions: reduced lifetimes across spectrum and reduced group velocities (especially 1–8 THz), leading to shorter MFPs. Differences between methods (BTE vs QHGK) for analogous 136-atom calculations attributed to finite-size/replica size effects.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Reported at 300 K only in the detailed analysis; no T-dependence curve shown for this composition in text.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Section IV.B; Fig. 3 (comparison panels a–e) and Table I (lists BTE kappa = 33.0 W/mK).

extracted_data.name_full: 15% Ge-substituted Type-II clathrate (Si116Ge20) — QHGK on replicated 5x5x5 supercell (Gamma-only) with interpolated lifetimes
extracted_data.brief_description: Quasi-harmonic Green–Kubo (QHGK) calculation on a 5x5x5 replicated supercell (17000 atoms) of the 136-atom cell containing the 15% Ge substitutions; Gamma-only real-space QHGK with lifetimes interpolated from smaller explicit ALD calculations yields a kappa close to BTE for the replicated crystalline alloy.
extracted_data.material_system: Si116Ge20 (Si0.85Ge0.15) clathrate — replicated crystalline substituted cell
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: Type-II clathrate derived from 136-atom conventional cell, replicated 5×5×5 → 17000 atoms (still crystalline periodic replica), substitutions replicated
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: reported at 300 K (results presented for modal properties and cumulative kappa at 300 K); QHGK used on replicated supercell at Gamma point.
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: kappa_QHGK(300 K, 5×5×5 replicated) = 31.0 W m^-1 K^-1 (Gamma point QHGK on replicated 136-atom cell).
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity computed from QHGK (quasi-harmonic Green–Kubo) — modal generalized heat capacities, generalized velocities, and generalized lifetimes τ_{μμ'} used; quantum statistics for populations at 300 K.
extracted_data.method_category: QHGK (real-space ALD generalization of Green–Kubo), empirical IFCs from Tersoff used as force calculator
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff empirical potential (same as used for BTE calculations); IFCs computed via finite differences.
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: 5×5×5 replicated supercell (17000 atoms) used for Gamma-only QHGK; phonon lifetimes γ(ω) interpolated from explicit ALD calculation on a 3×3×3 system (3672 atoms) using third-order splines. Authors state result (31.0 W/mK) is slightly lower than BTE (33.0 W/mK) and that agreement indicates closeness to size convergence.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon linewidths γ_μ computed (or interpolated) used in τ_{μμ'} Lorentzian; quantum statistics used. No explicit 4-phonon or separate mass-scattering model invoked (disorder included via explicit substitution in supercell and full IFCs).
extracted_data.alloy_modeling_approach: Explicitly replicated substituted cell (periodic replication of 136-atom substituted cell) — includes local mass and force-constant disorder within the cell but retains long-range periodicity of the replicated pattern.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: QHGK (replicated, 5×5×5) = 31.0 W/mK vs BTE (136-cell, RTA) = 33.0 W/mK; small discrepancy attributed to size-scale effects. For true random alloy (see next entry) QHGK on large explicit random supercell yields dramatically lower kappa.
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: No direct experimental comparison for this computational alloy; authors use comparison with BTE to validate QHGK for crystalline/partially disordered systems.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Small difference between QHGK and BTE attributed to finite-size/replica effects; QHGK is formally equivalent to BTE-RTA for crystals but offers real-space approach convenient for large disordered supercells.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Reported at 300 K; authors note QHGK and BTE equivalence formally and that QHGK classical limit reproduces MD results up to relatively high T in prior studies, but no T sweep for this specific composition reported.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Section IV.B; Fig. 4 (panels a–e) compares 136-atom replicated and randomly substituted 17000-atom models; Table I lists QHGK value 31.0 W/mK for the replicated substituted clathrate.

extracted_data.name_full: Si0.85Ge0.15 random-alloy Type-II silicon clathrate — QHGK on explicit 17000-atom random-alloy supercell
extracted_data.brief_description: QHGK calculation of thermal conductivity on an explicit 5×5×5 replicated supercell in which Si atoms were randomly substituted by Ge to create a realistic random alloy (17000 atoms); predicts a dramatic reduction of kappa due to long-range disorder affecting generalized phonon velocities and diffusivities.
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: Type-II clathrate, 5×5×5 replicated supercell (17000 atoms) with random substitution of Si by Ge (realistic random alloy without long-range periodicity of substitution)
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: reported at 300 K (main reported value); modal analyses at 300 K shown in Fig.4.
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: kappa_QHGK(300 K, random alloy, 17000 atoms) = 1.7 W m^-1 K^-1 — a ~200× reduction relative to crystalline diamond Si and a large drop compared to the substituted replicated crystalline cell (31 W/mK).
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity from QHGK (quasi-harmonic Green–Kubo), using generalized heat capacities c_{μμ'}, generalized velocities v_{μμ'}, and Lorentzian generalized lifetimes τ_{μμ'} (γ_μ linewidths interpolated from smaller calculations). Quantum statistics used at 300 K.
extracted_data.method_category: QHGK (real-space ALD applicable to disordered systems), empirical IFCs from Tersoff used for force constants
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff empirical potential used to compute IFCs and forces for the large explicit alloy; third-order splines used to interpolate lifetimes from smaller-system ALD calculations.
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: 17000-atom supercell (5×5×5 replication of conventional cell) with random substitution of Ge atoms. Lifetimes γ(ω) interpolated from explicit ALD calculation on a 3×3×3 system (3672 atoms) using third-order splines; QHGK performed at Gamma point for large cell. Authors assert the 17000-atom system is close to size convergence.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Three-phonon linewidths (γ) used to form τ_{μμ'} Lorentzian; disorder is explicitly present in masses and force constants in the large supercell. No mention of additional scattering terms like 4-phonon or electron-phonon for this calculation.
extracted_data.alloy_modeling_approach: Explicit random substitution in a large supercell (real-space random-alloy model) — includes both mass disorder and force-constant disorder; contrasts with periodic replicated substituted cell.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: kappa_random_QHGK(17000 atoms) = 1.7 W/mK vs kappa_QHGK(replicated periodic substituted cell) = 31.0 W/mK (same nominal composition) — authors attribute large difference to long-range disorder effects and reduction in generalized phonon diffusivity, especially for low-frequency modes (<3 THz).
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: No direct experimental measurement for this specific random-alloy clathrate reported in paper.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Long-range random disorder dramatically reduces generalized phonon velocities and diffusivity (v_{μμ'}), particularly for low-frequency, long-wavelength modes; this is the main cause of the ~20× reduction between replicated substituted cell and truly random alloy (and ~200× reduction relative to crystalline diamond Si). Authors emphasize that DOS and lifetimes are similar, but diffusivity D(ω) is strongly suppressed by long-range disorder.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Reported at 300 K only. Authors note that low-frequency modes (<3 THz) contribute most to the difference in kappa between replicated crystalline alloy and random alloy; no explicit temperature sweep provided.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Section IV.B; Fig. 4 (panels a–e show DOS, phase-space, lifetimes, diffusivity, cumulative kappa); Table I lists QHGK value 1.7 W/mK for Si0.85Ge0.15 random clathrate.

The Physics of Phonons

extracted_data.brief_description: Equilibrium MD (EMD) predictions of lattice thermal conductivity for bulk Si1-xGex alloys constructed as explicit alloy supercells (x = 0.00–1.00), used to validate the interatomic potential and EMD parameters versus literature; values reported/ plotted and compared to experiment and first-principles results.
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: cubic diamond bulk alloy; explicit random alloy supercells constructed (12 × 12 × 12 periodic UC^3 for validation)
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: not explicitly stated for the validation dataset shown in Figure 2(b); temperature dependence for selected structures studied at 200, 300, 400, 500 K elsewhere in paper (see temperature section)
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: Plotted in Figure 2(b) and described as 'in the same order' as experimental and other theoretical works; no single-tabled numerical list in text for all x. (Paper states their kappa data match literature order-of-magnitude.)
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity (kappa_L) computed via equilibrium MD using the Einstein relation (mean-square-displacement of energy moment); electronic contribution excluded.
extracted_data.method_category: empirical-potential MD (equilibrium MD)
extracted_data.md_flavor: EMD using Einstein relation (time-integrated heat current / energy-moment MSD); implemented in LAMMPS
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff potential (cited Tersoff 1989); used for Si–Ge interactions (no alternate parameterization given)
extracted_data.emd_gk_details: Einstein relation formulation used (Equation (1)); production in NVE ensemble; time step 0.5 fs; relaxation 500 ps prior to runs; each data point is average of 10 independent simulations, each at least 4 ns long; R_mu is time-integration of heat current (following Kinaci et al. approach). No thermostat during production (NVE). No explicit mention of quantum corrections.
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: Validation alloy cell: 12 × 12 × 12 periodic unit cells (UC^3). Time step 0.5 fs; equilibration 500 ps; production ≥4 ns per run; 10 runs averaged. No explicit finite-size extrapolation procedure described for bulk alloy validation.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Anharmonic phonon–phonon scattering naturally included via MD; mass-disorder (explicit atomic species) and boundary/interface scattering if present in the cell; isotope scattering not separately treated; no explicit 4-phonon or electron-phonon terms beyond what MD dynamics produce.
extracted_data.alloy_modeling_approach: Explicit atomic mixing: random/constructed alloy supercells with the stated compositions; relaxed lattice parameters used to construct alloy structures.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: Paper states their EMD/Tersoff bulk-alloy kappa values are 'in the same order' as experimental and theoretical studies (references given) but does not tabulate numerical deviations; used this comparison as validation of potential and EMD parameters.
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: Authors report qualitative agreement ('in the same order') with experimental datasets cited ([14,50,51]) for bulk alloys; no tabulated % errors provided.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Not explicitly enumerated for the bulk-alloy comparison, but elsewhere authors note differences with experiment can arise from pristine simulation cells lacking vacancies/dislocations/impurities and from model limitations (classical MD vs quantum effects not explicitly discussed).
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: Temperature dependence for selected structures studied at 200–500 K: general trend is kappa decreases with increasing temperature due to increased phonon–phonon (Umklapp) scattering; some heavily suppressed systems (e.g., x=0.5 nanowires or certain superlattice periodicities) show near temperature-independence between 200–500 K.
extracted_data.key_figures_tables_locations: Figure 2(a) (lattice parameters) and Figure 2(b) (thermal conductivity of bulk alloys compared to literature); temperature-dependent data appear in Figure 6 (selected structures).

extracted_data.name_full: Symmetric and asymmetric crystalline Si–Ge bulk superlattices (EMD/Tersoff predictions)
extracted_data.brief_description: EMD calculations of lattice thermal conductivity for symmetric and asymmetric Si/Ge bulk superlattices along different growth directions (<001>, <111>) studying periodicity (w), number of interfaces, and interface roughness effects; non-monotonic dependence on period attributed to wave–particle crossover of phonons.
extracted_data.composition_x: Implicitly 50–50 per-layer in symmetric superlattices (equal Si and Ge UC per sublayer) and various ratios in asymmetric (e.g., 12-36 UC etc.), overall Si and Ge contents vary depending on structure
extracted_data.structure_and_phase: Diamond cubic Si and Ge layers stacked to form periodic superlattices; symmetric: equal Si/Ge UC per period; asymmetric: unequal layer thicknesses; relaxation applied prior to property calculation.
extracted_data.temperature_points_K: Room temperature (explicit kappa-p vs periodicity shown). Selected superlattices also included in temperature sweep at 200, 300, 400, 500 K (Figure 6 panels for symmetric and asymmetric bulk superlattices).
extracted_data.thermal_conductivity_values: Lowest bulk superlattice kappa along growth direction reported ≈5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (pristine), reducible to ≈3 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ with interface roughness; transverse directions show larger reductions with roughness (up to 50%). Non-monotonic dependence on period: minima found at specific periodicities (e.g., w=8 in <111> and w=12 in <001>, corresponding to N=4).
extracted_data.kappa_definition_and_components: Lattice thermal conductivity (kappa_L) computed by EMD via Einstein relation; electronic contributions not included.
extracted_data.method_category: empirical-potential MD
extracted_data.md_flavor: EMD (Einstein relation/heat-moment MSD) in LAMMPS, NVE production runs
extracted_data.interatomic_potential: Tersoff potential (cited Tersoff 1989) used for Si–Ge interactions
extracted_data.emd_gk_details: Einstein relation for thermal conductivity (Equation (1)); NVE ensemble for production; time step 0.5 fs; systems relaxed for 500 ps; each reported data point is an average of 10 simulations each ≥4 ns. Interface roughness introduced by modeling diffusion zones (Fick's law) of 0.28–1.0 nm (2–8 atomic layers).
extracted_data.simulation_cell_and_convergence: Example geometry: symmetric superlattice 12 × 12 UC^2 cross-section (~42.5 nm^2) with length 48 UC (~26.5 nm) in <001>; another geometry 7 × 8 UC^2 (~30 nm^2) with length 32 UC (~30.5 nm) in <111>. Periodicity parameter w = l/N described; number of interfaces varied (2,4,8,16,l). No explicit extrapolation to infinite cross-section; periodic boundary conditions applied in growth direction for superlattice; for bulk kappa all directions set periodic.
extracted_data.phonon_scattering_mechanisms_included: Anharmonic phonon–phonon scattering from MD; interface scattering explicitly studied; mass-disorder included where alloying/diffusion zones are modeled; boundary scattering via finite cross-sections for nanowires but not for bulk periodic directions.
extracted_data.alloy_modeling_approach: Interfaces with graded composition (diffusion zones) modeled using Fick's law to mimic annealed/rough interfaces; composition ratio preserved while introducing intermixing over specified lengths.
extracted_data.reported_method_comparisons: Authors compare trends qualitatively with experimental superlattice studies and cite theoretical works (e.g., Dames & Chen, Savic et al.). They note anomalous (non-monotonic) kappa vs period behavior that they attribute to wave–particle crossover, a physics explanation rather than a methodological artifact.
extracted_data.agreement_with_experiment: Authors state that their lowest bulk superlattice kappa (≈3–5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ depending on roughness) is close to experimentally observed superlattice kappa; remaining differences attributed to pristine simulated layers lacking defects/vacancies/dislocations and other real-sample imperfections.
extracted_data.proposed_reasons_for_discrepancies: Differences with experiment attributed to pristine simulation cells without vacancies/dislocations/impurities, ideal interfaces; method-driven factors discussed qualitatively include the role of interface roughness, periodicity (wave vs particle transport), and mass disorder; classical MD limitations (e.g., lack of quantum corrections) are not explicitly invoked as main reasons in text.
extracted_data.notes_on_temperature_dependence: For selected bulk superlattices, kappa generally decreases with increasing temperature (200–500 K) due to stronger phonon–phonon scattering, but some structures near minimum-kappa periodicities show weak temperature dependence between 200–500 K.

theory-1.name: Method-as-Effective-Scattering Operator (MESO) Theory (revised)
theory-1.description: Predicted lattice thermal conductivity κ for crystalline Si, Ge, and Si1-xGex is controlled by phonon heat capacities, group velocities and the effective phonon collision operator (scattering). Different computational methods (empirical-potential MD with EMD/GK/Einstein or NEMD; empirical-potential ALD/PBTE using IFCs from a potential; first-principles PBTE with differing levels of scattering physics such as isotope, 4-phonon, electron–phonon, and differing BTE solvers RTA vs iterative) can be interpreted as implementing different approximations to (i) the harmonic spectrum and (ii) the total scattering operator. MESO reframes method choice as selecting an “effective scattering operator” plus an “effective phonon spectrum”; method-to-method κ(T) differences are then predictable by identifying which physical scattering channels are omitted/added and by diagnosing spectrum errors (v, phase space, Grüneisen/anharmonicity). Numerical artifacts (finite-size in MD, NEMD gradient/thermostat effects) are treated as additional effective scattering channels that can bias κ downward, partially compensating intrinsic potential-driven upward bias.
theory-1.theory_query: Build theories of how the choice of method (Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber empirical potentials in molecular dynamics, Green-Kubo or nonequilibrium MD, first-principles phonon Boltzmann transport with DFT force constants) changes the predicted lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline silicon, germanium and Si1-xGex, as a function of temperature, based on the following results.

components.theory_name_plain_language: Each method behaves like it adds/removes phonon-scattering channels and reshapes phonons
components.theory_description: Predicted lattice thermal conductivity κ for crystalline Si, Ge, and Si1-xGex is controlled by phonon heat capacities, group velocities and the effective phonon collision operator (scattering). Different computational methods (empirical-potential MD with EMD/GK/Einstein or NEMD; empirical-potential ALD/PBTE using IFCs from a potential; first-principles PBTE with differing levels of scattering physics such as isotope, 4-phonon, electron–phonon, and differing BTE solvers RTA vs iterative) can be interpreted as implementing different approximations to (i) the harmonic spectrum and (ii) the total scattering operator. MESO reframes method choice as selecting an “effective scattering operator” plus an “effective phonon spectrum”; method-to-method κ(T) differences are then predictable by identifying which physical scattering channels are omitted/added and by diagnosing spectrum errors (v, phase space, Grüneisen/anharmonicity). Numerical artifacts (finite-size in MD, NEMD gradient/thermostat effects) are treated as additional effective scattering channels that can bias κ downward, partially compensating intrinsic potential-driven upward bias.
components.theory_description_plain_language: Methods disagree mainly because they (1) predict different phonon speeds and (2) include different amounts/types of phonon scattering (real or artificial). If you know what scattering a method misses or adds, you can often predict whether it will over- or under-predict κ and how this changes with temperature.

law.theory_statement: For bulk crystalline Si and Ge (diamond-cubic) and substitutional bulk Si1-xGex, differences between methods in predicted lattice κ(T) are dominated by differences in the effective total phonon scattering rate (collision operator) and, secondarily, by differences in harmonic phonon spectra. To first order in method differences, κ_method(T) can be compared by an effective Matthiessen-like decomposition of inverse lifetimes, 1/τ_eff = Σ_i 1/τ_i, where i spans at least intrinsic 3-phonon, 4-phonon, isotope/mass-defect, alloy/disorder, electron–phonon (when doped), and boundary/finite-size/numerical-artifact contributions. Methods that omit an important τ_i channel at a given T tend to overpredict κ at that T; methods that introduce extra numerical dissipation (e.g., NEMD thermostat/gradient artifacts or insufficient size/time convergence in MD) tend to underpredict κ relative to a well-converged, physics-complete reference.
law.theory_statement_plain_language: Method-to-method κ differences can usually be explained by which scattering mechanisms are included or missing (plus any artificial scattering from the simulation setup).
law.domain_scope: Bulk crystalline Si and Ge and bulk substitutional Si1-xGex (not nanowires/superlattices where boundary/interface dominates), phonon-dominated heat transport. Applies when comparing: (a) PBTE/ALD calculations with specified included scattering terms; (b) classical MD (EMD/GK/Einstein or NEMD) using empirical potentials; (c) hybrid PBTE workflows where forces/IFCs come from ML surrogates of DFT. Not intended for strongly localized transport regimes where a lifetime picture breaks down.
special_cases: Low-T regime (well below Debye temperature): classical MD uses equipartition and therefore has incorrect mode heat capacities; MESO must be augmented with quantum-statistics corrections or restricted to T where classical approximations are acceptable.

Strong disorder/localization (some alloys, highly disordered configurations): a simple perturbative τ_alloy term can fail; explicit-disorder real-space formalisms (large-supercell QHGK/MD) may be required.
When comparing to experiment: experiments include additional extrinsic scattering (defects, boundaries) and may include electronic κ; comparisons must match the definition (lattice-only vs total).

supporting_evidence.text: First-principles Si PBTE shows adding 4-phonon scattering lowers κ at 300 K by ~8% (3ph-only overestimates); and 4ph importance grows with T, with stated scaling τ_3ph ~ T^-1 and τ_4ph ~ T^-2, producing increasing high-T corrections.

First-principles Si PBTE (Pheasy+ShengBTE iterative for 3ph; FourPhonon RTA for 4ph) reports κ_3ph(300 K) ≈125.4 W/mK and κ_3+4ph(300 K) ≈115.4 W/mK (7.9% drop), demonstrating an omitted channel changes κ systematically.

Electron–phonon interaction (EPI) in Si at 300 K can reduce lattice κ by up to ~45% at extreme carrier concentrations (~1e21 cm^-3), showing that adding an additional scattering channel can strongly reduce κ when relevant (doped case).

Empirical Tersoff-IFCs used in ALD/BTE for bulk diamond Si yield κ_Q(300 K)=305 W/mK versus DFT-PBTE inversion κ(300 K)=147 W/mK, consistent with a method/potential that effectively yields weaker scattering and/or higher velocities (i.e., different effective collision operator/spectrum).

A SW force-matched potential used in EMD-GK MD for pristine bulk Si gives κ(300 K)=207±12 W/mK and the authors attribute overprediction vs experimental literature primarily to the potential choice, illustrating method bias due to effective spectrum/scattering differences set by the force field.

First-principles PBTE literature/review emphasizes that empirical potentials can deviate due to dispersion/anharmonicity errors; MD has finite-size issues and classical statistics; PBTE differs by RTA vs iterative solution choices—explicitly linking method discrepancies to spectrum/scattering/operator approximations.
Si PBTE direct inversion vs RTA differs by ~5% at 300 K (147 vs 140 W/mK), showing that even within PBTE, solver approximations change the effective collision-operator treatment and κ.

ALD/PBTE with DFT forces vs HDNNP forces yields nearly identical κ(300 K) for Si (112.1 vs 110.4 W/mK) within the same PBTE-RTA workflow, indicating that if the force/IFC source preserves the scattering operator and spectrum, κ agreement follows—supporting the MESO focus on operator/spectrum fidelity rather than implementation brand.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Scattering-rate additivity (Matthiessen-like) and the sensitivity of κ to included scattering channels (3ph/4ph/isotope/EPI) and to RTA vs iterative PBTE are established concepts in phonon transport.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A method-centric unification: treating *both* physical omissions (e.g., no 4ph) and numerical artifacts (finite-size/thermostats/gradients) as contributions to an effective scattering operator, enabling sign and temperature-trend predictions for cross-method bias (MD vs empirical-ALD vs DFT-PBTE).
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: The ingredients are known, but the explicit synthesis into a predictive framework for method bias (including numerical artifacts as effective scattering terms) goes beyond typical per-method discussions.
references: Broido (2007) Intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity of semiconductors from first principles [PBTE framework; channel decomposition baseline]
Feng (2016-2018) Four-phonon scattering in semiconductors [temperature scaling and importance of 4ph]
Turney (2009-2012) Thermal conductivity from MD and lattice dynamics; potential sensitivity [method/potential bias concepts]
McGaughey (various) Green–Kubo MD thermal conductivity [MD convergence/finite-size/algorithmic sensitivity]

law.statement_name: High-T divergence law: omission of 4ph causes increasing κ overprediction with T
law.theory_statement: In bulk crystalline Si (and by analogy Ge), for temperatures where intrinsic anharmonic scattering dominates (typically above ~0.5 ΘD), methods that include only 3-phonon scattering (or that effectively emulate only 3ph physics) will increasingly overpredict lattice κ(T) relative to methods that include both 3ph and 4ph scattering, because 4ph rates rise faster with temperature (reported scaling τ_3ph ~ T^-1 versus τ_4ph ~ T^-2 in Si). Consequently, the ratio κ_3ph-only(T)/κ_3ph+4ph(T) increases with T over the high-T range.
law.theory_statement_plain_language: Leaving out four-phonon scattering makes κ too high, and the error grows as temperature increases.
law.domain_scope: Bulk crystalline Si (explicit evidence) and likely Ge; temperature regime where intrinsic phonon–phonon scattering dominates and 4ph becomes comparable (hundreds of K up to ~1500 K for Si as studied). Applies to PBTE/ALD approaches; MD may or may not mimic 4ph depending on potential fidelity but still follows the principle that stronger high-order anharmonicity lowers κ.
special_cases: If extrinsic scattering dominates (strong alloy disorder, defects, boundaries), adding 4ph may have a smaller relative effect on total κ.

If a workflow uses temperature-dependent effective IFCs (renormalization) that partially absorb 4ph effects into effective 3ph rates, the monotonicity can be weakened though the general trend remains toward lower κ when true 4ph is included.

supporting_evidence.text: First-principles Si PBTE study reports τ_3ph ~ T^-1 and τ_4ph ~ T^-2; inclusion of 4ph becomes significant above ~500–700 K and 3ph-only at 900 K gives κ≈43 W/mK and is ~20% larger than measurement, i.e., omission yields growing high-T overprediction.
Independent first-principles PBTE study shows at 300 K 4ph already reduces κ by ~7.9% (125.4→115.4 W/mK), establishing a nonzero correction that is expected to grow with T.

Review-level discussion notes four-phonon scattering can be comparable to three-phonon even for low-anharmonicity materials like Si and Ge near/above ΘD, implying increasing relevance at high T and thus growing bias if omitted.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: The increasing importance of 4ph scattering with T is known.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: Formulating this as a cross-method divergence rule (a monotonic bias-with-T diagnostic) to anticipate how a 3ph-only workflow will depart from a 3+4ph reference across temperature.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: It is a repackaging of known scaling into an actionable method-bias prediction.
references: Feng (2016-2018) Four-phonon scattering in Si [establishes scaling and high-T corrections]
ShengBTE/FourPhonon literature [demonstrates κ reduction with 4ph]

law.statement_name: Empirical-force-field bias law: κ inflation via (v, τ) co-bias in bulk Si
law.theory_statement: For bulk diamond-cubic Si around room temperature and above, an empirical potential that (i) over-stiffens acoustic branches (inflating group velocities v) and/or (ii) underestimates anharmonic scattering strength (inflating τ by reducing effective anharmonicity/phase space) will systematically overpredict κ relative to DFT-based PBTE benchmarks, because κ ≈ Σ c_qν v_qν^2 τ_qν is multiplicatively sensitive to both v and τ. In practice, the evidence indicates Tersoff-derived IFC ALD/BTE can yield ~2× larger κ than DFT-PBTE at 300 K, consistent with simultaneous spectrum and scattering bias.
law.theory_statement_plain_language: If the force field makes phonons too fast or too long-lived (or both), κ comes out too large, sometimes by about a factor of two.
law.domain_scope: Bulk, defect-free diamond Si; comparisons between (a) empirical-potential-derived ALD/PBTE and (b) DFT-PBTE (iterative or inversion) in the ~300 K regime (and higher where phonon–phonon dominates). Not a claim about all empirical potentials; it is a conditional diagnostic when such spectrum/anharmonic biases exist.
special_cases: An empirical potential can be tuned to match κ at a particular T yet still have incorrect mode-resolved contributions and wrong κ(T) slope.
In nanostructures (pores, grain boundaries, superlattices, nanowires), boundary/interface scattering can dominate and mask bulk spectrum/anharmonic errors.

supporting_evidence.text: Tersoff-based ALD/BTE for diamond Si yields κ_Q(300 K)=305 W/mK (and κ_classical=260 W/mK) while DFT-PBTE inversion yields κ_Q,Inv(300 K)=147 W/mK (and DFT classical limit ≈123 W/mK), demonstrating large κ inflation from Tersoff-derived lattice dynamics.

Pristine Si EMD-GK using a force-matched SW potential yields κ(300 K)=207±12 W/mK and authors state overprediction vs experimental reference is mainly due to the interatomic potential, supporting the idea that force-field choice changes effective spectrum/scattering and thus κ.

First-principles uncertainty study shows κ(300 K) is strongly sensitive to phonon properties like TA sound speed and Grüneisen parameters (correlations R^2 up to 0.89), consistent with the mechanism that biases in velocities/anharmonicity produce large κ shifts; it also shows XC functional choice shifts κ from ~122 (LDA) to ~171 (BEEF-vdW) W/mK at 300 K for isotopically pure Si (3ph-only), indicating multiplicative sensitivity to spectrum/anharmonicity descriptors.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Empirical potential dependence of κ is widely recognized.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: A portable diagnostic that emphasizes *co-bias* in v and τ as the dominant driver of order-unity κ inflation, explicitly tying it to factor-of-two discrepancies observed for Tersoff-derived ALD/BTE in Si.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: Mechanism is standard but the explicit “co-bias” framing is a useful synthesis rather than a new physical law.
references: Turney (2009-2012) Potential sensitivity of κ in Si [empirical-potential dependence]
Jain & McGaughey / Broido PBTE benchmarks [DFT reference κ and mode dependence]

new_predictions_likely: For bulk diamond Si at 300 K, a well-converged MD (EMD or homogeneous NEMD with finite-size handled) using Tersoff-1989 will predict κ larger than an ab initio PBTE benchmark that includes at least isotope scattering (and especially if it includes 4ph), with κ_Tersoff/κ_DFT likely >1.3; a factor near ~2 is plausible if the MD result reflects the same Tersoff spectral/anharmonic biases seen in Tersoff-ALD/BTE.

For bulk Si at ~1100 K, if the ab initio reference includes 4ph scattering, a Tersoff-1989 MD prediction is likely to be higher by >30% unless NEMD setup artifacts (strong gradients/short length) artificially suppress κ.

For Si PBTE workflows, swapping DFT forces for a high-quality surrogate trained to DFT (e.g., HDNNP) while keeping the same ALD/BTE settings will preserve κ(T) within a few percent over the training-valid range (e.g., 200–500 K), as long as the surrogate reproduces both harmonic and cubic IFCs accurately.
new_predictions_unknown: In bulk Si1-xGex near x≈0.5 at 300–500 K, the spread between empirical-potential MD and first-principles DFPT+VCA/Tamura PBTE may shrink in relative terms compared to pure Si because alloy disorder dominates scattering; however, if force-constant disorder/localization is strong, explicit-disorder methods (large-supercell QHGK/MD) could predict substantially lower κ than VCA/Tamura PBTE.

For Ge, empirical-potential bias sign may be less consistent than for Si because TA branch features are sensitive to force-constant range; potentials that misplace TA(X) could either increase or decrease κ relative to ab initio even if they are reasonable for Si.
negative_experiments: Compute Tersoff-1989 vs DFT mode-resolved group velocities and anharmonic indicators (e.g., Grüneisen parameters or 3ph phase space) for bulk Si; if Tersoff does not systematically increase v and/or increase τ (via reduced anharmonicity) yet still yields much larger κ, then the “(v,τ) co-bias” mechanism is incomplete and implementation/solver effects dominate.

Run size- and time-converged EMD and homogeneous NEMD for bulk Si with the same Tersoff-1989 potential; if both converge to κ within ~10–20% of DFT-PBTE (3ph+isotope or 3ph+4ph+isotope), then the theory’s claim that the potential’s effective operator/spectrum is the dominant bias source for Tersoff must be revised (suggesting ALD/BTE extraction or other workflow differences are the main source).

For Si PBTE, compare κ from iterative PBTE vs RTA across 200–500 K for the same IFCs; if differences become large (>15–20%) already at 300 K, then MESO must weight solver-induced operator errors more strongly than currently assumed for Si.

unaccounted_for.text: No direct bulk Tersoff-1989 MD κ values for *bulk* Si at 300 K and 1100 K are provided in the evidence set; thus quantitative calibration for the specific 'GPUMD homogeneous NEMD' scenario is not directly supported here (only indirect evidence from Tersoff-ALD/BTE and other potentials).

conflicting_evidence.text: A cited discussion summarizes that prior work found GK-MD and BTE consistent for pure Si and Ge, which could appear to conflict with strong 'empirical potentials overpredict' narratives; this is likely reconciled by potential choice differences and convergence details, but the evidence here does not specify which potentials/method settings produced that consistency.

Some first-principles PBTE-RTA results for Si (DFT LDA, small IFC supercells, RTA) can yield κ(300 K) around ~112 W/mK, which is below common ~150 W/mK benchmarks; this indicates that method bias is not always in the direction of overprediction and that convergence/approximations (supercell size, RTA) can also suppress κ.

special_cases: Definition matching: some ab initio works report isotopically pure κ and omit isotope scattering; others include natural isotope scattering (and/or 4ph). Comparisons must align which channels are included.

High-T intrinsic Si: total κ includes a growing electronic component; when comparing lattice-only methods (MD, phonon PBTE) to experimental total κ, the electronic contribution can cause apparent discrepancies not due to phonon physics.
Alloys: VCA/Tamura-type alloy scattering may miss force-constant disorder and nonperturbative effects; explicit-disorder supercells can produce much lower κ (seen in clathrate random-alloy example).

references: Broido (2007) Intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity of semiconductors from first principles [PBTE; scattering operator/channel picture]
Feng (2016-2018) Four-phonon scattering and thermal transport in semiconductors [importance of 4ph and temperature scaling]
Turney (2009-2012) Predicting phonon properties/thermal conductivity from interatomic potentials [potential sensitivity; MD vs LD]
McGaughey (2004-2013) Green–Kubo MD for κ and convergence issues [MD finite-size/time and methodological artifacts]
existing_theory.what_already_exists: Channel decomposition, Matthiessen-like reasoning, solver-approximation impacts (RTA vs iterative) and empirical potential sensitivity are well known.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: A unified, method-bias predictive framing that explicitly treats numerical artifacts as effective scattering channels on the same footing as physical channels, to anticipate sign and temperature dependence of κ bias across MD/NEMD, empirical-ALD, and DFT-PBTE.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: It is a new synthesis/use of existing phonon-transport concepts rather than a fundamentally new transport law.

components.mission_statement:
The theories will be used to answer the following questions before the corresponding simulation results are seen. Address the mechanisms they depend on:


H5. Pure crystalline Si: Tersoff-1989 GPUMD homogeneous NEMD kappa versus
almaBTE (160.5 W/mK at 300 K, 40.5 W/mK at 1100 K).
Value: ratio Tersoff/almaBTE at 300 K. Category for 1100 K:
"agree within 30 %", "Tersoff higher by more than 30 %",
"Tersoff lower by more than 30 %".

theory-2.name: Spectrum-and-Statistics Consistency (SSC) Theory
theory-2.description: SSC theory posits that across Si/Ge/SiGe, the dominant cross-method deviations in κ(T) can be decomposed into (1) spectrum fidelity (harmonic dispersion, especially acoustic branches that control v and phase space) and (2) statistics fidelity (Bose–Einstein vs classical equipartition, plus solver fidelity for the linearized BTE). It predicts systematic temperature windows where each error source dominates: at low-to-intermediate T, wrong statistics and RTA-vs-iterative differences can be significant; at high T, statistics differences diminish but anharmonic-order completeness (4ph) dominates; and across all T, an inaccurate empirical potential spectrum can impose a persistent multiplicative bias.
theory-2.theory_query: Build theories of how the choice of method (Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber empirical potentials in molecular dynamics, Green-Kubo or nonequilibrium MD, first-principles phonon Boltzmann transport with DFT force constants) changes the predicted lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline silicon, germanium and Si1-xGex, as a function of temperature, based on the following results.

components.theory_name_plain_language: κ differences come from phonon spectrum errors and wrong thermal populations
components.theory_description: SSC theory posits that across Si/Ge/SiGe, the dominant cross-method deviations in κ(T) can be decomposed into (1) spectrum fidelity (harmonic dispersion, especially acoustic branches that control v and phase space) and (2) statistics fidelity (Bose–Einstein vs classical equipartition, plus solver fidelity for the linearized BTE). It predicts systematic temperature windows where each error source dominates: at low-to-intermediate T, wrong statistics and RTA-vs-iterative differences can be significant; at high T, statistics differences diminish but anharmonic-order completeness (4ph) dominates; and across all T, an inaccurate empirical potential spectrum can impose a persistent multiplicative bias.
components.theory_description_plain_language: To predict κ well you need (a) the right phonon dispersions and (b) the right temperature-dependent phonon populations; different methods get these right or wrong in different temperature ranges.

law.statement_name: Statistics-convergence law: quantum vs classical κ discrepancy shrinks with T
law.theory_statement: For bulk crystalline Si modeled with the same scattering physics (3ph) and solver class, the difference between κ computed with quantum Bose–Einstein phonon populations and κ computed in the classical (equipartition) limit decreases with increasing temperature, approaching zero at sufficiently high T. Therefore, classical MD (which is classical by construction) is expected to deviate most from quantum PBTE at low-to-moderate temperatures and to become more comparable at high temperatures, provided the underlying force field/IFCs are otherwise consistent.
law.theory_statement_plain_language: Classical methods are most wrong at low temperature; they get closer to quantum results at high temperature.
law.domain_scope: Bulk crystalline Si (direct evidence) and similar non-polar crystalline semiconductors (e.g., Ge) when comparing otherwise similar scattering physics; excludes regimes where additional physics (4ph, electrons, strong disorder) dominates.
special_cases: Even at high T, classical MD can still disagree due to force-field errors and finite-size artifacts; convergence in statistics does not guarantee accuracy.
At low T, hydrodynamic/normal-process effects can also make RTA less accurate, compounding differences.

supporting_evidence.text: DFT PBTE study reports κ_Q,Inv(300 K)=147 W/mK and κ_Cl,Inv(300 K)=123 W/mK and notes quantum and classical results converge as T increases (Fig. 2 trend).

Review discussion emphasizes classical MD uses equipartition and requires quantum corrections at low T; prior quantum-correction attempts can fail, highlighting a statistics-driven method discrepancy at low T.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: Quantum-vs-classical occupation effects are well known.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: Positioning this as a method-selection rule for κ(T) comparisons among MD and PBTE for Si/Ge with explicit expectation of temperature windows where the discrepancy is largest/smallest.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: It is a structured application of known behavior to cross-method forecasting.
references: Broido (2007) PBTE for semiconductors [quantum statistics baseline]
McGaughey (MD literature) [classical MD limitations and quantum correction discussions]

law.statement_name: Solver-fidelity law: RTA underestimates κ relative to inversion/iterative PBTE when mode coupling matters
law.theory_statement: Within PBTE for crystalline Si, replacing a full solution of the linearized BTE (direct inversion/iterative) with single-mode RTA reduces κ by a method-dependent fraction because RTA neglects off-diagonal coupling in the collision operator; the underestimation is modest for Si near room temperature (~few percent) but becomes larger at lower temperatures where normal-process/hydrodynamic effects are more important.
law.theory_statement_plain_language: RTA is usually a little low for Si at room temperature and can be more wrong at low temperature.
law.domain_scope: Bulk crystalline Si (explicit evidence), PBTE frameworks with 3ph scattering; extrapolates qualitatively to Ge; not aimed at strongly disordered alloys or nanostructures.
special_cases: In some complex crystals (example clathrate) off-diagonal corrections can be <1%; thus RTA error is material- and spectrum-dependent.

supporting_evidence.text: For diamond Si at 300 K, inversion gives 147 W/mK while RTA gives 140 W/mK (~5% lower), demonstrating solver-dependent κ differences in Si.
The Si 3ph-only PBTE study notes literature indicating iterative vs RTA differences <4% for Si at room temperature, consistent with modest solver bias at RT.
For the Si136 clathrate, authors report RTA corrections beyond RTA are <1%, illustrating a boundary condition where RTA error is very small due to collision-operator structure in that material.

novelty_evaluation.what_already_exists: RTA vs iterative/inversion differences are well known in PBTE.
novelty_evaluation.what_is_novel: Explicitly combining solver choice with temperature-window logic for cross-method bias forecasting.
novelty_evaluation.classification_explanation: An organizing rule rather than a new discovery.
references: Omini & Sparavigna (1996) iterative PBTE [solver theory baseline]
Broido/Esfarjani PBTE works [RTA vs iterative comparisons]

new_predictions_likely: If a PBTE κ(T) curve for bulk Si is recomputed with inversion/iterative instead of RTA using identical IFCs and scattering mechanisms, κ will increase by only a few percent near 300 K but by a larger fraction at lower T (e.g., <200 K).

Two workflows with identical scattering physics but different harmonic dispersion fidelity (e.g., different potentials) will show κ differences that correlate with acoustic sound speeds and TA-branch features (SSC predicts stronger correlation than with details like IFC extraction algorithm).
new_predictions_unknown: For Ge, if a potential reproduces acoustic sound speeds but mispredicts TA(X), SSC predicts that κ differences will show up primarily through changes in phase space and lifetimes rather than group-velocity magnitude alone; this could invert the sign of κ bias depending on how phase space shifts.

In Si1-xGex, SSC predicts the temperature at which classical and quantum κ converge depends on alloy-induced spectral broadening; strong disorder may make classical MD appear ‘closer’ to quantum PBTE at lower T than in pure Si because high-frequency modes are already suppressed.
negative_experiments: Compare κ(T) from PBTE using DFT IFCs with κ(T) from classical-limit PBTE using the same IFCs; if the difference does not decrease with T, SSC’s statistics-convergence premise is violated for the tested regime.

For Si, test whether κ differences across XC functionals correlate with TA sound speed and Grüneisen parameter as reported; if correlations fail in an expanded dataset, SSC’s spectrum-dominance claim needs revision.

unaccounted_for.text: The provided evidence set includes many nanowire/superlattice κ values dominated by boundary/interface scattering; SSC is formulated for bulk crystalline comparisons and does not attempt to explain these boundary-dominated results.

special_cases: Polar materials (e.g., GaN in the HDNNP paper) require long-range electrostatics; SSC as written is tuned to non-polar group-IV crystals like Si/Ge.
If κ is dominated by extrinsic scattering (alloy disorder, boundaries), spectrum/statistics improvements may have limited impact on κ magnitude.

references: Broido (2007) Intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity of semiconductors from first principles [quantum statistics and PBTE; spectrum importance]
Gunnarsson/Heine style phonon occupation discussions [quantum vs classical heat capacity effects in solids]
Omini & Sparavigna (1996) iterative PBTE [solver fidelity effects]
existing_theory.what_already_exists: The roles of quantum statistics, harmonic dispersion fidelity, and PBTE solver approximations are established.
existing_theory.what_is_novel: Packaging these into a temperature-windowed, cross-method forecasting theory targeted to MD vs PBTE comparisons in Si/Ge/SiGe.
existing_theory.classification_explanation: Mainly a synthesis/organization of known effects rather than a new mechanism.
